::: callout-note
**Living document.** This describes the data pipeline (`crxp-data/`) that produces every indicator
served by the CRXP app. Update it whenever stages, the warehouse schema, sources, the config model, or
the handoff contract change. Companions: *Application Technical Documentation* (`crxp/docs/`) and
*Methodology Guide* (this folder). Methodological detail (formulas, definitions) lives in the
Methodology Guide; this document covers **engineering**.
:::

# Overview & goals

`crxp-data` is an open-source, reproducible **Python** pipeline that turns public data into reviewed,
tract-level indicators (with margins of error) and hands them to the CRXP app. Goals:

- **Config-driven:** add/modify indicators by editing YAML — little or no code.
- **Uncertainty-aware:** every estimate carries a 90% MOE; CV and a reliability flag are derived.
- **Comparable over time:** ACS 5-year overlap handled; pre-2020 vintages harmonized to 2020 tracts.
- **Multi-source:** one ingester module per source (ACS, CDC PLACES, …) behind a common interface.
- **Reproducible & documented:** runnable by analysts/students; no ArcGIS. Dependencies are pinned
  in `pyproject.toml`, a **`provenance.json`** (library + GDAL/PROJ versions) ships with each build, and
  the warehouse parquets are committed so `--reexport` works on a fresh clone.
- **Two products:** the app **data contract** (handoff) and a reusable **warehouse** (parquet + DuckDB).

Runs on Python 3.11+ (tested on 3.14). Pinned deps include pandas, pyarrow, duckdb, requests, pyyaml,
geopandas, shapely, pyproj, rasterio, exactextract (raster stack), plus pytest for tests.

# End-to-end architecture

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph Sources
    ACS["Census ACS API<br/>or Census Reporter"]
    CDC["CDC PLACES<br/>Socrata"]
    NLCD["USGS NLCD<br/>MRLC WCS"]
    VIIRS["EOG VIIRS VNL<br/>night lights"]
  end
  ACS --> ING["Ingest<br/>sources/*.py"]
  CDC --> ING
  NLCD --> ING
  VIIRS --> ING
  ING --> HARM["Harmonize<br/>2010 to 2020 tracts<br/>harmonize.py"]
  HARM --> CALC["Indicator calc<br/>MOE / CV / reliability<br/>indicators/calc.py"]
  CALC --> SP["Spatial<br/>z, breaks, LISA + FDR<br/>spatial.py"]
  SP --> WH[("Warehouse<br/>parquet + crxp.duckdb<br/>warehouse.py")]
  SP --> EXP["Export / handoff<br/>export_crxp.py"]
  EXP --> APP["crxp/static/data<br/>app data contract"]
  CFG["config/*.yml"] -. drives .-> ING & HARM & CALC & EXP
```

# Data flow (per indicator)

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as analyst
  participant B as build.py
  participant S as sources
  participant H as harmonize
  participant C as calc
  participant SP as spatial
  participant W as warehouse
  participant E as export
  U->>B: run build for an indicator
  B->>S: fetch indicator variables
  S-->>B: raw vars by geoid and year
  B->>H: harmonize 2010 to 2020 tracts (ACS only)
  H-->>B: raw on 2020 tracts
  B->>C: compute value, MOE, CV, reliability
  B->>B: keep 2020 tracts and per-area density if needed
  B->>W: write warehouse (parquet, duckdb)
  B->>B: comparable-period change and significance
  B->>SP: z-scores and LISA per year
  B->>E: build value file, analytics, aggregates
  E->>E: merge into app on handoff
```

# Repository structure

```
crxp-data/
├─ config/
│  ├─ region.yml                 # 14 counties, ACS settings, reliability thresholds, vintages
│  ├─ sources/<id>.yml           # source registry (provider, cadence, sustainability)
│  └─ indicators/<slug>.yml      # one file per indicator (THE main editing surface)
├─ src/crxp_data/
│  ├─ config.py                  # load_region / load_indicator / list_indicators
│  ├─ sources/
│  │  ├─ census_acs.py           # ACS ingester (API + Census Reporter; raw variables; retries)
│  │  ├─ cdc_places.py           # CDC PLACES ingester (Socrata; joins on locationid)
│  │  ├─ raster_nlcd.py          # NLCD / Tree Canopy zonal stats (exactextract; atomic downloads)
│  │  └─ viirs.py                # EOG VIIRS night-lights zonal mean (atomic downloads)
│  ├─ harmonize.py               # 2010→2020 tract crosswalk + raw-variable allocation
│  ├─ indicators/calc.py         # MOE propagation, CV, reliability, value assembly, significance
│  ├─ spatial.py                 # z-scores, quantile breaks, kNN weights, local Moran/LISA + BH-FDR
│  ├─ geo.py                     # tract representative-point centroids + 2020 tract land area
│  ├─ qa.py                      # build-failing QA gate (coverage / null-rate / value range)
│  ├─ provenance.py              # captures lib + GDAL/PROJ versions → provenance.json
│  ├─ warehouse.py               # parquet + DuckDB writers
│  ├─ aggregate.py               # county + region rollup (authoritative county estimates + pooled region)
│  ├─ export_crxp.py             # app contract builders (schemaVersion, aggregate MOE) + atomic handoff
│  └─ build.py                   # CLI orchestrator (per-indicator, --handoff/--reexport/--reharmonize)
├─ data/                         # committed reference data (area + population crosswalks, land area)
├─ warehouse/                    # tract_indicators/*.parquet + county_indicators/*.parquet (COMMITTED) + crxp.duckdb (gitignored)
├─ exports/                      # generated: app contract staging (gitignored)
├─ scripts/                      # seed_acs_indicators*.py, build_pop_crosswalk.py, helpers
├─ tests/                        # pytest (calc, spatial+FDR, export, harmonize, qa, geo)
└─ docs/                         # this doc + methodology guide + working paper
```

# Configuration model

Three YAML layers, all loaded by `config.py`.

## `region.yml`
Region-wide settings: the 14 `counties` (FIPS/name/state), `crs`, `tract_vintage: 2020`, the ACS
block (`provider`, `api_base`, `annual_years`, `comparable_years`, **`tract2010_years`**), and
`reliability` thresholds (`cv_caution: 15`, `cv_unreliable: 30`, `z_90: 1.645`).

## `sources/<id>.yml`
Registry metadata for each raw source: `fetch` mode, native geo level, `vintages`, `cadence`,
`update_status`, `last_release`, `decommission_risk`. Used for documentation/sustainability (see the
catalog) and provenance.

## `indicators/<slug>.yml` — the main editing surface
One file per indicator. Common fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Stable numeric id (used as the contract filename and warehouse key) |
| `slug`, `label`, `description`, `meta_why` | Identity + human copy (drive metadata page) |
| `theme` | App category key (must exist in the app manifest `categories`) |
| `format`, `decimals` | `percent` / `dollar` / `number` / `years`; display precision |
| `higher_is_better` | `true` / `false` / `null` (drives direction language) |
| `source` | `acs` or `cdc_places` |
| `acs` / `cdc` | Source-specific spec (below) |

### ACS spec (`acs:`) by `kind`

| `kind` | Fields | Value computed |
|---|---|---|
| `median` | `estimate_var`, `moe_var` | passthrough estimate + MOE (also used for averages, indices) |
| `count` / `number` | `estimate_var`, `moe_var` | passthrough count (+ `per_land_area: true` → divide by sq-mi land area for density) |
| `proportion` | `num_vars[]`, `num_moe_vars[]`, `den_var`/`den_vars[]`, `den_moe_var`/`den_moe_vars[]`, optional `multiplier` | summed numerator ÷ denominator; subset-safe proportion MOE |
| `rate` | same as proportion | numerator ÷ denominator where numerator ⊄ denominator; ratio MOE |

`num_vars`/`den_vars` are **lists** (summed), so derived measures (e.g. cost burden = several income
bands; child poverty with a 6-line denominator) are pure config. Variable ids are official ACS codes
(`B19013_001E` estimate, `B19013_001M` margin). Subject tables (`S####`) are auto-routed to the
`/acs/acs5/subject` endpoint. An optional `num_vars_by_year` (with `num_moe_vars_by_year`) overrides the
numerator for specific vintages, for the rare table whose category boundaries shift across releases
(B25034 "year structure built"; see the methodology guide's *Homes built since 2010*).

### CDC spec (`cdc:`)
`measure_id` (e.g. `OBESITY`) + `data_value_type` (default `Crude prevalence`). The ingester pulls the
model-based estimate and 95% CI, converted to a 90%-equivalent MOE.

### Tract-file spec (`tract_csv:`) — bring your own data
Any CSV keyed by census-tract GEOID becomes an indicator through `source: tract_csv`
(`sources/tract_csv.py`). Fields:

| Key | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | yes | CSV path relative to the `crxp-data` root, or an `https://` URL |
| `geoid_col` | yes | Column holding tract GEOIDs (read as text, zero-padded to 11 digits; a trailing `.0` is stripped) |
| `value_col` | yes | Column holding the value |
| `kind` | yes | `count`, `proportion`, `rate`, `median`, or `index` |
| `source_label` | yes | Credit shown in the app, the metadata page, and the download bundle |
| `year` / `year_col` | exactly one | A single data year, or a column of years for multi-year files |
| `moe_col` | no | A 90% MOE column; enables CV and reliability flags |
| `tract_vintage` | no (2020) | `2010` allocates to 2020 tracts with the crosswalk |
| `pop_col` | for 2010 `proportion`/`rate` | 2010-tract population used to weight the allocation |
| `source_url` | no | Link for the metadata page's resources |
| `source_id` | no (`tract_csv`) | Warehouse `source_id` |

Rows outside the region's counties are dropped; no matching rows, a missing column, or a duplicate
(geoid, year) stops the build with a message naming the problem. So does a vintage mismatch: if more than
5% of the in-region GEOIDs are not tracts of the declared `tract_vintage` (checked against the committed
crosswalk), the build stops and suggests the other vintage when most of the misses belong to it. On 2010 tracts, counts are allocated by
allocation factor and rates/proportions by population-weighted pseudo-counts
(`harmonize_places_rates`); medians and indices are rejected. County and region values are derived from
the tracts (see *County + region rollup*), and the manifest entry carries `countyMethod: "derived from tracts"`.

# Pipeline stages

## Ingest — `sources/`
`census_acs.fetch_indicator(region, indicator, years)` returns a tidy frame of **raw ACS variables**
by `(geoid, year)`. Provider resolves from `region.acs.provider`:

- `auto` → official **API** if `CENSUS_API_KEY` is set, else **Census Reporter**.
- `api` — multi-vintage history; requires the key; per-year/county requests with **retry + backoff**. If a
  table is genuinely absent for a vintage (all counties fail identically) the year is skipped (non-fatal);
  a partial failure (some counties returned, others didn't) raises rather than silently publishing
  a truncated year that would corrupt the series.
- `census_reporter` — keyless but **latest release only** (single year). Good for quick refreshes.

`cdc_places.RELEASES` is a registry of the six PLACES releases (2020–2025), each specifying its
Socrata dataset ID and tract vintage (`2010` or `2020`). `fetch_measure(region, measure_id, dv_type,
level, releases=None)` queries one release at a time, joins on the canonical **`locationid`** (tract
FIPS), guards confidence-bound order, and returns `value` + a 90%-equiv `moe` tagged with its source
vintage. `newest_wins(df)` then de-duplicates across releases, keeping the most recent release's
estimate per `(geoid, data_year)`.

In `build.py`, the CDC branch passes 2010-vintage tract rows through
`harmonize_places_rates(raw, crosswalk, years_2010)` (2020-native rows pass through untouched) and feeds
the merged frame into the shared `calc` engine; county releases are stitched newest-release-wins directly
(county boundaries are stable). On export, `manifest_entry` sets **`crossReleaseTrend: true`** plus a
`trendNote` for every `cdc_places` indicator; the app keys off this flag to suppress change figures
(significance markers, the report *Change* column, county-card deltas) while still drawing the level
series and its band. For the pseudo-count allocation math and why PLACES cannot support trend analysis,
see the *Methodology Guide* §CDC PLACES time series (and CDC's *Using the Data* guidance).

`raster_nlcd.fetch_indicator` (source `raster`) clips region GeoTIFFs from the **MRLC WCS** (auth-free,
EPSG:5070, cached under `data/raster/`, gitignored) and computes **area-weighted zonal statistics** to
2020 tracts with `exactextract` (`stat: classfrac` or `mean`); no sampling MOE (`moe=None`). For the
exactextract method and why rasters carry classification accuracy rather than a sampling MOE, see the
*Methodology Guide* §Raster-derived indicators. Needs the geo stack
(`rasterio`, `geopandas`, `exactextract`, `pyproj`, `shapely`). Indicator config carries a `raster`
block (`coverage_template` with `{year}`, `years`, `stat`, and `classes` for `classfrac`). It also
supports **local raster sources** (e.g. NLCD Tree Canopy Cover): a `raster` block with `outer_zip` +
`inner_zip_template` + `tif_template` reads per-year GeoTIFFs straight from a (nested) zip via GDAL
`/vsizip/`, clips once to the region (reprojecting tracts to the raster CRS), caches the small clip, and
takes the zonal `mean`.

`viirs.fetch_indicator` (source `viirs`) produces **light pollution** = area-weighted **mean radiance**
per tract from the **EOG VIIRS VNL V2** annual composites. EOG downloads are account-gated (Keycloak
realm `eog`); the global GeoTIFFs are obtained **manually** (drop a `*_<year>_*median_masked*.tif.gz`
into `data/raster/` from a browser-authenticated EOG session) or via the EOG OAuth API
(`EOG_USERNAME`/`EOG_PASSWORD` + a per-account `EOG_CLIENT_ID`/`EOG_CLIENT_SECRET`), then clipped to the
region (`/vsigzip/` windowed read) and cached. Config: a `viirs` block (`version`, `years`).

## Harmonize — `harmonize.py` / `cdc_places.harmonize_places_rates`
ACS years in `tract2010_years` (2014–2019) use **2010 census tracts**. `build_crosswalk` returns the
**population-weighted** crosswalk `data/tract_2010_2020_crosswalk_pop.csv` when present (built by
`scripts/build_pop_crosswalk.py` from the Census 2010↔2020 **block** comparability files + 2020 block
population — drop the `TAB2010_TAB2020_ST*.zip` files in `data/raster/`), otherwise falls back to the
area-weighted `tract_2010_2020_crosswalk.csv`. `to_2020_tracts` allocates each raw variable to 2020
tracts by the crosswalk `afact` weights. To re-process the 2010-vintage years after changing the
crosswalk: `build … --reharmonize` (re-fetches only 2014–2019, merges with 2020+ from the warehouse).
For the dasymetric allocation math, the population-vs-area rationale, and the median caveat, see the
*Methodology Guide* §Geographic harmonization.

`harmonize_places_rates(raw, crosswalk, years_2010)` applies population-weighted pseudo-count
allocation to 2010-vintage PLACES rows (2020-native rows and county data pass through unmodified). See
the *Methodology Guide* §CDC PLACES time series for the derivation.

## Indicator calc — `indicators/calc.py`
`compute_indicator` assembles `value` + `moe` per the `kind`, then derives `cv` and `reliability`.
Pure scalar functions (`proportion_moe`, `ratio_moe`, `agg_moe`, `cv_percent`, `reliability`,
`significant_diff`) implement the Census formulas (unit-tested against worked values). For value+CI
sources (CDC), `add_reliability` adds CV/reliability directly.

## Spatial — `spatial.py`
Per year: `zscores`, cross-year-consistent `quantile_breaks`, `knn_weights` (k=8 from tract
representative-point centroids), and `local_moran` → LISA quadrant codes with **Benjamini–Hochberg FDR**
correction. `spatial.py` is the **single source of truth** for LISA; the app consumes the precomputed
quadrants and no longer recomputes them client-side. For the conditional-permutation null, the
representative-point rationale, and the FDR procedure, see the *Methodology Guide* §Spatial statistics.

## Warehouse — `warehouse.py`
Writes one parquet per indicator and upserts into the DuckDB table `tract_indicators` (delete-then-
insert by `indicator_id`). It also stores the **`county_indicators`** rollup (one parquet per indicator
under `warehouse/county_indicators/`, geoid = county FIPS plus a `REGION` row) so `--reexport` can rebuild
aggregates without re-fetching. See schema below.

## County + region rollup — `aggregate.py`
`build_county_region` produces the **authoritative** county and region values (not a tract average),
each source through its own path: ACS county tables (`census_acs.fetch_indicator_county`), the CDC PLACES
county model (`cdc_places.fetch_indicator_county`, dataset `swc5-untb`), or land-area-weighted tract
values for raster/VIIRS, all run through the same `calc` engine. Region pooling uses `_sum_raw` (sum
estimates, MOEs in quadrature) and `census_acs.county_population` weights for medians/indices. Output is
one frame per indicator persisted to the `county_indicators` warehouse. For the aggregation policy (why
not average tracts) and the median approximation caveat, see the *Methodology Guide* §County and region
estimates.

`tract_csv` sources have no published county estimate, so `_tract_derived` builds county and region
values from the tracts: counts are summed (MOEs in quadrature); every other kind is a population-weighted
mean of tract values, weighted by tract population from the committed `total-population` warehouse
(nearest available year). Tracts without a value or a population weight are skipped for weighted kinds.
For counts, a county (or region) total is published only when every expected 2020 tract in it has a value;
otherwise the total is left empty, because a sum over some tracts is not a total.

## Export / handoff — `export_crxp.py`
Builds the app contract: value file (with `schemaVersion`, `moe`/`cv`/`reliability`), z + LISA docs, and
county/region **aggregates including `regionMoe`/`countyMoe`**, now consuming the authoritative
`county_indicators` rollup (`build_aggregates`) rather than averaging tracts. With `--handoff`,
`merge_into_app` writes them into `crxp/static/data`, **merges** the indicator into `manifest.json`
(+ `schemaVersion`) and `aggregates.json` via **atomic temp-file writes**, writes `meta/m<id>.md`, and emits
**`provenance.json`** (library + GDAL/PROJ versions). All file reads/writes use explicit UTF-8 encoding
(config YAML, contract JSON, and meta markdown) so non-ASCII characters survive on Windows.

## Orchestration — `build.py`
`python -m crxp_data.build <slug…> [--handoff] [--reexport] [--refetch] [--reharmonize]` runs the stages
per indicator and prints a summary (coverage, comparable-period change & significance counts, files
written). A **QA gate** (`qa.py`) runs before the warehouse write and **fails the build** on collapsed
geoid coverage, excessive nulls, or out-of-range values. ACS builds are **incremental by default** — only
years missing from the warehouse are fetched, then merged (`--refetch` forces a full re-fetch).
**`--reexport`** rebuilds the app contract from the committed warehouse without any fetch (e.g. after
changing export/period/analytics logic); **`--reharmonize`** re-fetches + re-harmonizes only the
2010-vintage years (after a crosswalk change). Comparable-period endpoints are derived dynamically as
`{latest, latest−5, latest−10}` from `annual_years`, so adding a year advances both comparisons.

## CDC PLACES breadth staging — `scripts/stage_cdc_all.py`

This utility script is separate from the main build pipeline and runs independently. It stages
the full PLACES catalogue — all 40 measures at both tract and county level, across all six
releases, newest-release-wins, with 2010-vintage tract rows harmonized to 2020 tracts (2020-native
rows pass through) so every staged file is on the app's 2020-tract geography — into `warehouse/cdc_raw/`:

```
warehouse/cdc_raw/
  tract/<MEASUREID>.parquet      # one file per measure; all data years; 2020-tract geography
  county/<MEASUREID>.parquet     # one file per measure; all data years; county FIPS
  catalog.csv                    # decision aid: per (measure × level) category, year span,
                                 #   and latest-year reliability counts
```

`catalog.csv` surfaces category, available year span, and latest-year reliability counts for each
measure × geography combination, designed as a review aid for deciding which measures to promote
into the app manifest. Staging touches **no indicator configs or app manifest** and does not trigger
a handoff, so it is safe to re-run at any time without side effects.

Currently 16 of the 40 measures are surfaced in the app (the indicators in the catalog above).
The remaining 24 are held in `cdc_raw/` pending analyst review of coverage and comparability.

# Warehouse data model

**`tract_indicators`** (DuckDB `warehouse/crxp.duckdb` + `warehouse/tract_indicators/<id>.parquet`):

| Column | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `geoid` | varchar | 2020 census tract |
| `indicator_id` | int | matches config + contract filename |
| `year` | int | endpoint year of the 5-year window |
| `value`, `moe`, `cv` | double | estimate, 90% MOE, coefficient of variation (%) |
| `reliability` | varchar | `ok` / `caution` / `unreliable` / null |
| `period_start`, `period_end` | int | 5-year window (ACS); `period_start = year − span` |
| `is_rolling` | bool | true for ACS rolling series; false for point estimates (CDC) |
| `est_method` | varchar | `acs_direct` / `cdc_places_mrp` / … |
| `source_id`, `source_vintage` | varchar | provenance |
| `redacted` | bool | reserved for small-n suppression |
| `created` | varchar | build date |

The DuckDB file is the **shared backend** groundwork: any app (CRXP, QoL, future) can query it with SQL.

```sql
-- example: most-uncertain tracts for an indicator
SELECT geoid, value, moe, cv, reliability
FROM tract_indicators
WHERE indicator_id = 30 AND year = 2024
ORDER BY cv DESC LIMIT 20;
```

# Sources & how to add one

Each source is a module in `sources/` exposing `fetch_indicator(region, indicator, years) -> DataFrame`.
To add a source:

1. Create `config/sources/<id>.yml` (provider, cadence, sustainability).
2. Implement `sources/<id>.py` returning either raw variable columns (ACS-style → `compute_indicator`)
   or a `value`/`moe` frame (CDC-style → `calc.add_reliability`).
3. Add a dispatch branch + `src_meta` (est_method/source_id/span/rolling) in `build.py`.
4. Add indicator YAMLs referencing `source: <id>`.

# Add a new indicator (standard operating procedure)

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["Write indicator config (YAML)"] --> B["Build the indicator"]
  B --> C{"Review summary and warehouse"}
  C -->|looks right| D["Hand off to app"]
  C -->|issues| A
  D --> E["Validate data contract"]
  E --> F["Build site and spot-check"]
```

1. **Write the YAML** (`config/indicators/<slug>.yml`). Pick `kind`; use official ACS variable codes.
   Bulk additions can be scripted (see `scripts/seed_acs_indicators*.py`, which encode verified codes).
2. **Dry run:** `python -m crxp_data.build <slug>` (no handoff). Check coverage (~752 tracts),
   reliability mix, and comparable-period change in the printout; inspect the warehouse.
3. **Hand off:** re-run with `--handoff`.
4. **Validate + view:** `cd ../crxp && npm run build:data`, then `npm run build` and spot-check.
5. Update the *Methodology Guide* indicator catalog and this doc if a new pattern/source was introduced.

::: callout-tip
Verify unfamiliar ACS variable codes against the group metadata
(`https://api.census.gov/data/<year>/acs/acs5[/subject]/groups/<TABLE>.json`) before adding them —
a wrong/absent code skips all years and yields empty output.
:::

# Review, QA & testing

- **QA gate** (`qa.py`, run in `build.py` before warehousing): **fails the build** if a year's geoid
  coverage collapses, the null rate is excessive, or finite values fall outside a configured plausible
  range, catching catastrophic ingest problems rather than silently publishing them.
- **QA reports** (`warehouse/qa/`, committed): every check writes `<slug>.json` (per-year coverage, null
  rate and row count; configured range; `pass`/`fail`; problems; date) and regenerates `qa_report.md`, one
  table across all indicators. A failing check writes its report before stopping the build.
  `python -m crxp_data.qa --all` (with `PYTHONPATH=src`) re-checks every indicator against the committed
  warehouse without fetching and exits non-zero if any fails.
- **Per-run summary** (build.py): geoid coverage, comparable-period significant-change counts, rows
  written, files merged: the first review surface.
- **Reliability flags:** CV-based `caution`/`unreliable` in the warehouse and contract; surfaced in
  the app. High-CV small-count rates are expected at tract level.
- **`pytest`** (`tests/`): MOE formulas + difference-significance vs Census worked values; spatial
  (z/breaks, **BH-FDR**, LISA false-positive control); export contract shape; harmonization allocation
  (counts, medians, pass-through); QA gate; representative-point centroids + crosswalk afact sums.
- **App contract gate:** `crxp/scripts/build-data.mjs` validates the handed-off files (schemaVersion,
  year-alignment, analytics/aggregate content, geoid reconciliation).
- **Visual checks:** Playwright spot-checks after handoff.

Run tests: `$env:PYTHONPATH="src"; .venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q` (or rely on `pyproject.toml`'s
`pythonpath=src`).

# Running the pipeline

```bash
# one-time
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
setx CENSUS_API_KEY <key>        # official ACS API (multi-vintage). Get one free at census.gov.

# run (Windows PowerShell; key inline if the shell hasn't picked up setx yet)
$env:CENSUS_API_KEY="<key>"; $env:PYTHONPATH="src"
.venv\Scripts\python -m crxp_data.build poverty-rate --handoff
```

Without a key, `provider: auto` falls back to Census Reporter (latest year only).

# Cadence & staggered updates

- **ACS** — annual rolling (latest endpoint 2024) + non-overlapping comparable years; re-pull on each
  ACS 5-year release.
- **CDC PLACES** — six releases (2020–2025) stitched into a newest-release-wins time series; data
  years 2017–2023 depending on measure. Add a new release by appending to `RELEASES` in
  `cdc_places.py` and re-running the affected slugs with `--handoff`.
- Updates are **per (source, indicator)**: re-run only the affected slugs with `--handoff`. County- or
  year-scoped gaps surface as no-data via the app's per-indicator availability handling. A formal
  run-ledger + manual-upload landing is a planned enhancement (P2.7).

# Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| `No ACS years could be fetched` | Wrong/absent variable code, or table missing all requested years — verify codes in group metadata |
| `! skipping <year>` | Table not published that vintage (e.g. C16002/B28002 pre-2016) — expected; non-fatal |
| All values null after build | Variable returns a Census jam value (`-888888888` "not available") at tract — that breakdown isn't published at tract level |
| `Missing Key` HTML from Census | `provider: api` without `CENSUS_API_KEY` |
| Coverage ~480 instead of ~749 | Harmonization not applied — confirm `tract2010_years` set and crosswalk present |
| `theme … not a manifest category` on handoff | Indicator `theme` must match an app manifest category key |
